At least 64 children have been killed and another 64 wounded since the fighting in Yemen escalated in early September, the United Nations’ Children Fund (UNICEF) said. "The number of casualties is likely to increase as renewed fighting continues around densely populated areas, particularly in Taiz and Lahj," UNICEF said. The UN body underscored that "basic services and infrastructure children depend on are also being directly impacted." At least seven schools and 28 health facilities, including five supported by UNICEF, have been damaged since the escalation began on September 3.

🎙 Araghchi: Regional security must be ensured without foreign interference 📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stressed that regional security must be ensured from within the region without foreign interference, highlighting discussions in Oman on preventing renewed war and establishing an independent regional security framework. Araghchi outlined the outcomes of his visit to Oman, including consultations on regional developments, efforts to prevent the war from reigniting, Muscat's diplomatic role, and the need to establish an independent regional security framework. ​ Speaking in an interview with local media, Araghchi said he had a very successful visit to Oman, during which he held fruitful meetings with his Omani counterpart and the Sultan of Oman. ​ In addition to the usual issues concerning bilateral relations, regional developments were also discussed during the visit, he said. ​ "American aggression and efforts to prevent the war from flaring up again were among the topics of our discussions. Iran's views on these issues are closely aligned with those of our Omani friends," Araghchi stated. ​ Referring to Oman's diplomatic role in regional developments, the foreign minister emphasized the country's contribution to diplomatic efforts. ​ "Oman was the first country to participate in these diplomatic efforts, and we are grateful for that. Muscat has always played a positive role in regional diplomacy and conflict resolution, and it continues to do so. We believe these efforts must continue," he said. ​ Araghchi also announced that discussions had been held on the need to establish a new and independent security framework in the region. ​ "We had constructive discussions in this regard. Across the region, there is a growing belief, stronger than ever before, that security must be ensured from within the region itself, without interference from foreign powers," he emphasized. ​ The Iranian foreign minister also referred to the trilateral meeting with the Foreign Minister of Uzbekistan during his visit to Oman. ​ "Considering Uzbekistan's geographical location in Central Asia, Oman's position in the Persian Gulf region, and Iran's location along the route connecting these two regions, we discussed issues related to transit and connectivity," Araghchi said. ​ Highlighting the substantive and detailed nature of the negotiations, he added: ​ "We discussed various issues during the meeting and agreed to continue our consultations and follow-up efforts to advance these matters." 📲 @Irna_en ​

US War Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a military cooperation agreement with Venezuela during his visit to Caracas, according to Venezuelan state television. Hegseth described the agreement as the "reestablishment of our defense partnership" and said it opens room for the "two great militaries" to work side by side. Venezuelan state television reported that Hegseth signed the agreement with Defense Minister Gustavo González López, with the deal reportedly intended to respect Venezuela’s "national sovereignty and independence." Delcy Rodríguez welcomed the resumption of technical and military ties, saying the agreement would provide training for Venezuelan troops, operational equipment and access to new technologies. Hegseth's visit follows a series of high-level US engagements with Venezuelan authorities focused on the country’s oil and mineral resources, and comes amid reports that the US is negotiating an agreement that could allow US troops to remain in Venezuela over the long term.
